prompt: Which statement best describes a share?

options.text: A loan to a company that must be repaid on a fixed date
A fixed deposit kept with a bank
A promise of a fixed monthly income

explanations.a: That describes a loan, such as a bond or a debt instrument. A share is not a loan.
explanations.c: A fixed deposit is money kept with a bank. A share is part-ownership of a company.
explanations.d: A share does not promise a fixed income. Its value and any dividends can change.

prompt: Hypothetical. A set has 30 questions and the pass mark is 85%. What is the fewest number of correct answers that passes the quiz part?
solution: 85% of 30 = 0.85 x 30 = 25.5. You cannot get half a question right, so round up to 26. Check: 26 / 30 = 86.7%, which passes. 25 / 30 = 83.3%, which does not.

prompt: You score 100% on the quiz. One own-words prompt has a point you did not tick. Does the gate count you as complete?

options.text: Yes. A perfect quiz score is enough.
No. Every prompt needs every required point ticked, and its text box must not be empty.
Yes, as long as you have typed at least one word in that prompt.
No, but only if the quiz score is below 85%.

explanations.a: The quiz is one part of the gate. The own-words prompts must also be complete.
explanations.c: Typing a word is not enough. Every required point must be ticked.
explanations.d: The quiz score does not change the own-words rule. A prompt with a missing point is not complete at any score.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "I passed Gate G1, so I can decide to trade with my savings now." Which part of this statement is wrong?

options.text: "I passed Gate G1". It is not possible to pass the gate.
"so I can decide to trade with my savings now". Passing measures educational competence only and does not say you should trade.

explanations.a: You can pass the gate by reaching 85% on the quiz and completing the own-words prompts. The first part of the statement can be true.
explanations.c: The statement is not correct. A pass shows understanding of the basics. It is not permission to trade with savings.

prompt: Hypothetical. A share has a bid of Rs 100 and an ask of Rs 101. What is the spread in rupees?
solution: Spread = ask - bid = 101 - 100 = Rs 1. The prices are hypothetical.

prompt: Which statements about the order book are correct? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Buy orders sit on the bid side.
The ask is the price a seller is asking.
The order book guarantees that the price will rise.
The spread is the gap between the bid and the ask.

explanations.c: The order book shows the orders waiting right now. It does not guarantee any future price move.
